primitives.name: Public Intelligence Route Deletion
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **What it does:** Deletes the entire `/intelligence` route tree (`apps/web/app/intelligence/*` — clv, engines, expected-points, metrics, opportunity-transfer, players pages) and strips references from nav, footer, sitemap, and other pages (academy, airwave, board, calibration, deck, gsn) plus related tests.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{\\text{int}}': 'Set of public intelligence routes', 'T_{\\text{ref}}': 'Set of reference points (nav, footer, sitemap)', 'T_{\\text{test}}': 'Set of test cases'}
primitives.assumptions: Routes and references are fully decoupled from public API surface.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Route tree deletion triggers cascading reference removal.

layer2.mapping: The deletion operation maps to a topological contraction in the web application graph, where nodes representing public routes are removed and edges representing cross-references are severed.

primitives.name: Rankings Link Removal
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **What it does:** Removes every nav link, footer link, CTA, and sitemap reference to `/rankings`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L_{\\text{rank}}': 'Set of ranking-related links', 'S_{\\text{ref}}': 'Set of site references (nav, footer, sitemap)'}
primitives.assumptions: Rankings functionality was never implemented and thus no backend logic needs preservation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Link references are stripped without affecting underlying systems.

layer2.mapping: Link removal is a derived kernel operation from the broader route deletion primitive, operating on a subgraph of the site’s navigation structure.
layer2.telemetry: No internal links point to `/rankings` post-deletion.

primitives.name: NGS Public Surface Removal
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **What it does:** Removes every *public* NGS route and reference.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{\\text{ngs}}': 'Set of public Next Gen Stats routes', 'R_{\\text{auth}}': 'Set of authenticated NGS routes'}
primitives.assumptions: Public NGS routes are distinct from internal ingestion endpoints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Public-facing NGS routes are isolated and removed while preserving internal APIs.

layer2.mapping: The operation mirrors a network partitioning task, where public NGS endpoints are severed from the public interface, leaving only internal access paths intact.

The intelligence route deletion (primitive 1) operates as a topological contraction, removing a connected component of the site’s routing tree and all associated references. This action is modeled as a set-theoretic operation on the public route space R_int, where R_int ⊂ R_web and all T_ref ∩ R_int = ∅ post-surgery. The rankings link removal (primitive 2) is a derived kernel of the former, acting on a subset of navigation links S_ref ⊆ R_int. The NGS surface removal (primitive 3) applies a similar principle but distinguishes between public and private API surfaces, ensuring R_ngs ⊂ R_web and R_auth ∩ R_ngs = ∅. Failure modes include residual references in cache or CDN, which are mitigated by verifying 404 responses and internal link integrity. Dualities emerge in that each surgery preserves internal data structures while erasing external accessibility, aligning with a functional separation of concerns in software architecture.
